en: half-brother; half-sibling; brother of the half blood

examples.ko: 제 이복형제는 저보다 세 살 많아요.
examples.en: My half-brother is three years older than me.

examples.ko: 드라마에서는 이복형제끼리 사이가 안 좋은 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: In dramas, half-siblings often don't get along.

examples.ko: 이복형제가 있다는 사실을 어른이 되어서야 알았어요.
examples.en: I only found out I had a half-brother after I became an adult.

examples.ko: 이복형제라도 어릴 때부터 같이 커서 정말 친해요.
examples.en: Even though we are half-brothers, we grew up together, so we're really close.
On holidays, the half-siblings all gather together too.

examples.ko: 이복형제 사이에서 재산 문제로 다툼이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A dispute over property arose between the half-brothers.

explain: 아버지는 같고 어머니가 다른 형제자매를 말하고, 일상에서는 '배다른 형제'라고도 해요. 어머니가 같고 아버지가 다른 경우는 '이부형제'라고 해서 구별해요. 부모의 재혼으로 생긴 '의붓형제'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to siblings who share a father but have different mothers, and in daily speech people also say '배다른 형제'. If the mother is the same and the father is different, the word is '이부형제'. It is also different from '의붓형제', who become siblings through a parent's remarriage.

examples.en: It was cold, so I pulled the edge of the blanket up to my chin.

examples.ko: 아이가 자는 사이에 이불자락이 바닥으로 흘러내렸어요.
examples.en: While the child slept, the edge of the blanket slipped down to the floor.

examples.ko: 이불자락 끝을 꼭 잡고 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: I fell asleep holding the end of the blanket tightly.

examples.ko: 엄마가 이불자락을 살짝 들추고 방에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Mom lifted the corner of the blanket slightly and came into the room.

examples.ko: 이불자락에 커피를 쏟아서 빨래를 해야 해요.
examples.en: I spilled coffee on the edge of the comforter, so I have to wash it.

examples.ko: 고양이가 이불자락 속으로 쏙 들어가 버렸어요.
examples.en: The cat slipped right under the edge of the blanket.

explain: '치맛자락', '옷자락'처럼 '-자락'이 붙은 말과 같은 계열이에요. 이불을 끌어올리거나 들추거나 붙잡는 동작과 함께 자주 나와요. 이불 전체는 '이불을 덮다/걷어차다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It belongs to the same family as '치맛자락' and '옷자락', which also use '-자락'. It often appears with actions like pulling up, lifting, or gripping the blanket. For the whole blanket, you say things like '이불을 덮다' or '이불을 걷어차다'.

examples.en: Hearing that story gives me a strange feeling.
There's a weird smell coming from the room.
The scene I saw in my dream was so strange.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 저를 이상야릇하게 쳐다봐서 불편했어요.
examples.en: That person looked at me in an odd way, so I felt uncomfortable.
It's a food with a strange taste, but I keep thinking about it.
Doesn't this picture look a bit strange?

explain: '이상하다'보다 느낌을 더 강조해서, 묘하고 낯설어서 딱 집어 말하기 어려운 기분이나 분위기에 써요. 기분, 냄새, 표정, 분위기와 잘 어울려요. 비슷한 말로 '야릇하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It adds more emphasis than '이상하다', and fits a feeling or atmosphere that is oddly unfamiliar and hard to pin down. It goes well with words like mood, smell, expression, and atmosphere. '야릇하다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 이상주의가 강해서 현실을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: My friend is very idealistic, so he doesn't understand reality well.

examples.ko: 젊을 때는 누구나 이상주의에 빠지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: When you're young, it's easy for anyone to fall into idealism.

examples.ko: 그는 이상주의자라서 돈보다 꿈을 먼저 생각해요.
examples.en: He's an idealist, so he thinks of dreams before money.

examples.ko: 너무 이상주의적으로 생각하지 말고 현실도 봐요.
examples.en: Don't think so idealistically; look at reality too.
I'm torn between idealism and realism.
This novel criticizes idealism.

explain: 반대말은 '현실주의'예요. 사람을 말할 때는 '이상주의자'라고 하고, '현실을 모른다'는 약간 부정적인 느낌이 들 때도 있어요. '이상적이다'(가장 바람직하다)와는 쓰임이 달라요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '현실주의' (realism). For a person you say '이상주의자', and it can sometimes carry a slightly negative feeling of being out of touch with reality. It differs from '이상적이다', which means ideal in the sense of most desirable.

examples.ko: 그에게 이 섬은 꿈에 그리던 이상향이에요.
examples.en: To him, this island is the utopia he dreamed of.

examples.ko: 사람들은 모두가 행복한 이상향을 꿈꿔 왔어요.
examples.en: People have always dreamed of a utopia where everyone is happy.
A utopia may not exist in reality.
That village looks as peaceful as a utopia.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기 속 이상향에서는 아무도 굶지 않아요.
examples.en: In the utopia of old tales, nobody goes hungry.
Everyone has a different idea of utopia.

explain: '유토피아'나 '지상낙원'과 비슷해요. 보통 '그리다', '꿈꾸다'와 함께 쓰고, 현실에는 없는 곳이라는 느낌이 있어요. 마음속에 그리는 이상적인 세계를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is close to 'utopia' or '지상낙원' (paradise on earth). It is usually used with '그리다' or '꿈꾸다', and carries a feeling of a place that does not exist in reality. It suits talk about an ideal world pictured in one's mind.

examples.en: I confessed everything in front of the teacher.
If you come clean about the truth, I'll forgive you.

examples.ko: 동생이 컵을 깼다고 이실직고해서 안 혼났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling admitted to breaking the cup, so he didn't get scolded.
It's better to come clean even now.
As soon as Mom asks, the child confesses right away.

examples.ko: 이실직고하지 않으면 계속 마음이 불편할 거예요.
examples.en: If you don't come clean, you'll keep feeling uneasy.

explain: 그냥 '솔직하게 말하다'가 아니라 숨기던 잘못을 털어놓을 때 써요. 친구나 가족 사이에서 "이실직고해!"처럼 장난스럽게 다그치는 말투로도 들을 수 있어요. 법적인 느낌이 강한 '자백하다'보다 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is not just 'to speak honestly'; it is used when you own up to a fault you were hiding. Among friends and family you may hear it in a playfully pushy tone, like "이실직고해!". It can be used more lightly than '자백하다', which feels more legal.

examples.en: The twenty-four solar terms tell us about the changing of the seasons.
Ipchun is the first of the twenty-four solar terms.
My grandmother farmed in step with the twenty-four solar terms.

examples.ko: 이십사절기를 다 외우는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to memorize all twenty-four solar terms.
The food people eat differs a little with each solar term.
The twenty-four solar terms are marked on the calendar.

explain: 줄여서 그냥 '절기'라고도 해요. 입춘, 하지, 동지처럼 하나하나를 말할 때는 이름으로 불러요. 태양의 움직임을 기준으로 해서 해마다 양력 날짜가 거의 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is often shortened to just '절기'. Individual ones are called by their own names, such as 입춘, 하지, and 동지. They are based on the sun's movement, so the solar-calendar dates are almost the same every year.

examples.en: The public transportation usage rate is rising every year.
They held an event to raise the library usage rate.
The usage rate doubled compared to last year.

examples.ko: 이용률이 낮은 노선은 없어질 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Routes with a low usage rate might be discontinued.

examples.ko: 무인 가게 이용률에 대한 조사 결과가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The survey results on the usage rate of unmanned stores came out.
I summarized the change in the usage rate in a graph.

explain: 시설이나 서비스를 얼마나 쓰는지를 퍼센트로 말할 때 뉴스나 보고서에서 많이 써요. '-률/-율'은 앞말의 끝소리에 따라 달라요. '이용률', '성공률'처럼 ㅇ 받침 뒤에는 '률'을 쓰고, '참여율'처럼 모음 뒤에는 '율'을 써요. 소리는 [이용뉼]로 나요.
explain_en: It is used in news and reports when talking about how much a facility or service is used, usually as a percentage. The suffix '-률/-율' depends on the sound before it: after ㅇ as in '이용률' and '성공률' it is '률', and after a vowel as in '참여율' it is '율'. It is pronounced [이용뉼].

examples.en: Water is leaking from the joint of the water pipe.

examples.ko: 이음매가 거의 안 보이게 벽지를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put up the wallpaper so the seam is almost invisible.

examples.ko: 바닥 이음매 사이에 먼지가 잘 껴요.
examples.en: Dust easily gets stuck between the joints in the floor.
I filled the joint between the two boards with glue.
Please check whether the joint is sturdy.

examples.ko: 철로 이음매 부분에서 덜컹 소리가 나요.
examples.en: There's a clunking sound at the joint of the railway track.

explain: 물건과 물건이 이어지는 자리를 말해요. 옷감을 바느질해 이은 선은 보통 '솔기'라고 하고, 파이프, 벽지, 바닥처럼 이어 붙인 곳에는 '이음매'를 써요. 비유로 서로 연결되는 부분을 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to the spot where two things are joined. The stitched line in fabric is usually called '솔기', while '이음매' is used for pipes, wallpaper, floors and other joined parts. It can also be used figuratively for a connecting point.

examples.en: We will donate all the profit from the event.
This year's profit grew a lot compared to last year.
We decided to share the profit with the employees.
We use part of the profit for scholarships.
We bought books with the profit made at the bazaar.
You have to subtract the tax from the profit first.

explain: '이익'이 넓은 말이라면 '이익금'은 실제로 남은 돈의 액수를 가리켜서, 기부하거나 나누는 상황에서 잘 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '수익', '이윤'이 있어요. 반대되는 상황은 '손해'나 '적자'라고 해요.
explain_en: While '이익' is a broad word, '이익금' points to the actual amount of money left over, so it shows up in contexts like donating or dividing it. Similar words are '수익' and '이윤'. The opposite situation is called '손해' or '적자'.

examples.en: The kids keep waiting impatiently for Dad to come.
I'm anxiously waiting, hour by hour, for news of whether I passed.

examples.ko: 이제나저제나 하며 문자를 기다렸는데 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I kept waiting for a text, thinking it would come any moment, but it never did.

examples.ko: 그는 이제나저제나 연락이 올까 휴대폰만 봤어요.
examples.en: He just kept staring at his phone, wondering if a call would come any minute.

examples.ko: 버스가 이제나저제나 오나 하고 계속 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: I kept looking down the road, wondering when the bus would finally come.
Grandmother is waiting eagerly for her grandchild to arrive.

explain: 거의 항상 '기다리다'와 함께 써서, 언제 올까 조마조마하며 계속 기다리는 마음을 나타내요. 그냥 '기다리다'보다 초조하고 간절한 느낌이 더 커요. 주로 뒤에 '-나 하고' 같은 표현이 이어져요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with '기다리다' and shows the nervous feeling of waiting and wondering when something will come. It sounds more anxious and eager than plain '기다리다'. It is often followed by patterns like '-나 하고'.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 외국에서 온 이주자가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many migrants from abroad in this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 정부가 이주자를 위한 한국어 수업을 열었어요.
examples.en: The government opened Korean classes for migrants.
Migrants have a hard time finding a job at first.
I went to a group that helps migrant families.

examples.ko: 그분은 몇 년 전에 이 마을에 온 이주자예요.
examples.en: He is someone who moved to this village a few years ago.
We provide the information that migrants need.

explain: '이민자'는 주로 다른 나라로 옮겨 가 사는 사람을 말하고, '이주자'는 사는 곳을 옮긴 사람을 더 넓게 가리켜요. 뉴스나 공문서 같은 글에서 자주 보이고, 비슷한 말로 '이주민'도 있어요.
explain_en: '이민자' mainly refers to people who move to live in another country, while '이주자' covers people who have moved their place of residence more broadly. It is seen in writing such as news and official documents, and '이주민' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 그 애는 내 실수를 보고 이죽거렸어요.
examples.en: He sneered when he saw my mistake.
Stop sneering from the side and help me.
His sneering way of talking is really annoying.
My friend made snide remarks, and it made me angry.
I want to avoid people who tease with sneers.

examples.ko: 왜 내 얘기만 나오면 자꾸 이죽거려요?
examples.en: Why do you keep making snide remarks whenever I come up?

explain: 비꼬듯이 얄밉게 말하거나 비웃는 모습에 써요. 비슷한 말인 '빈정거리다'도 있고, '이죽대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. 듣는 사람이 기분 나쁜 부정적인 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: It describes talking in a mocking, annoying way, or sneering at someone. '빈정거리다' is a similar word, and '이죽대다' means the same. It is used in negative situations where the listener feels bad.

examples.en: Prices are rising while my pay stays the same, so it's a double burden.

examples.ko: 장마와 폭염이 겹쳐 농민들이 이중고를 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: With the rainy season and heat wave overlapping, farmers are suffering a double hardship.

examples.ko: 일도 하고 공부도 하느라 이중고에 시달려요.
examples.en: I'm struggling with the double burden of working and studying.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 데다 길까지 막혀 이중고였어요.
examples.en: It was a double whammy: it rained and the road was blocked too.
We didn't give up even in the midst of the double hardship.

examples.ko: 이중고가 되지 않게 미리 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to prepare ahead so it doesn't become a double burden.

explain: 서로 다른 어려움 두 가지가 한꺼번에 닥쳤을 때 써요. 보통 '이중고를 겪다', '이중고에 시달리다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 느낌의 말로 '설상가상'이 있는데, 이쪽은 안 좋은 일이 또 생겼다는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used when two different hardships hit at the same time. It usually appears as '이중고를 겪다' or '이중고에 시달리다'. A similar-feeling word is '설상가상', which is used to say that something bad happened on top of an existing problem.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 이중성을 알고 크게 실망했어요.
examples.en: I was very disappointed when I found out about his duplicity.

examples.ko: 겉과 속이 다른 이중성이 보여서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: I saw the duplicity of his outside differing from his inside, and it was scary.

examples.ko: 이중성 때문에 아무도 그를 믿지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of his duplicity, nobody trusts him.

examples.ko: 우리 인간의 이중성에 대해 이야기해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's talk about the duality of us humans.
Doesn't everyone have a little bit of duality?

examples.ko: 빛은 파동과 입자의 이중성을 가진다고 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned that light has a wave-particle duality.

explain: 사람에게 쓰면 겉과 속이 다르다는 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 반대로 과학에서는 한 대상이 두 가지 성질을 함께 가진다는 중립적인 뜻으로 써요. 비슷한 표현으로 '이중적이다'가 있어요.
explain_en: When used about a person, it carries a strongly negative feeling of being different inside and out. In science, on the other hand, it has a neutral meaning of one thing having two properties at once. '이중적이다' is a similar expression.
